zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
# 就業減少推遲升息預期，股市再創紀錄

## 就業意外轉弱，短天期美債受惠最多

7月非農就業減少23,000人，前期數據又大幅下修，顯示招聘比原先報告的更弱，美債因此反彈。2年期殖利率下降6個基點至4.19%，領先5年期的5個基點、10年期的4個基點及30年期的3個基點降幅。市場將9月聯準會升息機率，由公布前接近60%下修至約40%。

報告的弱勢不只在當月：5月及6月就業合計下修103,000人。但失業率反而隨勞動參與率下降，降至4.1%，薪資增速也放緩。就業減少與失業率降低並不矛盾，部分人退出勞動市場，使失業率維持低檔。數據降低了立即升息的必要性，卻尚未證明勞動供需已鬆到足以讓通膨回到目標。

風險市場歡迎聯準會多一些觀望空間。S&P 500上漲0.62%再創紀錄，Nasdaq 100上漲1.19%，VIX降至14.90。里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Tom Barkin形容就業處於脆弱平衡，認為薪資目前沒有增加物價壓力，但若通膨加速，仍保留升息選項。

油價卻上漲，沒有替債市提供更多通膨紓解。10年期殖利率降至4.65%，大部分來自實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.40%，通膨補償僅降1個基點至2.25%。市場仍完全計入年底前一次升息，下週大額美債標售也尚待買方承接。週五對短端的幫助，因此大於長端。

## 修正改變勞動圖像，接下來看CPI

曲線逆轉週四趨平，5年期殖利率降至4.35%，10年期4.65%，30年期5.19%。2s10s擴大2個基點至46，2s30s擴大3個基點至100。2至10年期一週下降9至10個基點，30年期降8個基點；但10至30年期仍比一個月前高10至14個基點。

當月減少23,000人、前兩月合計下修103,000人，都削弱了立即升息的理由。但參與率下降也是失業率降至4.1%的原因之一。薪資增速放緩有利通膨展望，卻不等於可用勞工全面增加，或產能壓力已明顯解除。

9月升息機率下降約20個百分點至約40%時，交易員平倉原本防範年底前兩次升息的SOFR選擇權部位。年底前一次升息仍完全計價，另有部位防範2027年第二次行動。調整主要在時間，而主席Kevin Warsh有限的前瞻指引，使每次數據仍可能大幅改變這個時間表。

今年沒有投票權的Barkin，為觀望提供了更清楚的理由。在低招聘環境下，他認為就業處於脆弱平衡，目前沒有薪資通膨，勞動市場對價格的推力不大。他前一週才說政策限制程度是難以判斷的問題，仍可能在通膨加速時支持升息。這沒有抹去7月三名官員主張升息25個基點的異議，而是解釋了為何就業轉弱可以讓聯準會先等價格數據。

紐約聯準銀行7月消費者調查也呈現混合訊號。1年期通膨預期由3.7%微降至3.6%，3年期維持3.3%，5年期維持3.0%。受訪者認為失業後找到新工作的機率升至46.2%，為今年最高；同時，更多人預期整體失業率上升，擔心自己失去工作的人也略增。對勞動市場的整體憂慮，尚未造成再就業信心崩落。

10年期實質殖利率下降3個基點，解釋了名目漲勢的大部分。損益兩平通膨率僅降1個基點，只收回週四4個基點升幅的一部分。近一個月實質殖利率仍高10個基點，通膨補償則未變。即使短期就業展望明顯下修，投資人仍要求比一個月前更高的實質報酬。

美債供給將提供另一項檢驗。下週二標售$580億3年期、週三$420億10年期、週四$250億30年期。標售前指示殖利率顯示，3年及10年期可能達2025年初以來最高標售水準；30年期約5.20%，高於2001年8月以來任何一次同年期標售結果。價格可能吸引買方，但實際需求仍未經標售證明。

策略師對財政部由評估未來發行「增加」改成「變化」的措辭，也有不同解讀。部分人認為，可縮減20年及30年期規模，把融資成長集中於2至10年期；另一些人則認為借款需求太大，長端減量不切實際。財政部尚未宣布任何縮減。調整年期可重新分配供給壓力，卻不會減少所需現金總額。

## 科技供給增加，再融資競爭也加劇

信用債參與反彈，LQD漲0.18%，HYG漲0.19%，JNK漲0.21%，長天期美國企業債指數約漲0.20%至0.22%。高收益基金一週流入$40億，為兩年最大，投機級利差也回到接近2026年最窄。整體信用風險需求強勁，並不妨礙重複發行對特定產業造成壓力。

摩根大通把2026年科技、媒體及電信發行預測，由$4,500億升至$5,400億。大型雲端業者預計占$3,170億，其中資料中心專案融資$850億；若已辨識的交易都推進，後者可能超過$1,000億。排除大型雲端業者的科技發行預估，幾乎由$780億倍增至約$1,460億，主要納入Nvidia的6月$250億發行。供給問題已超出單一週的交易日程。

既有債券顯示承接成本。投資人面對6、7月非預期的$750億供給，部分大型雲端業者利差擴大約15個基點，過去一週雖恢復，發行時間缺乏透明度仍是問題。Alphabet的2月30年期債，利差已超過美債100個基點，發行時約83，6月低點約70。新完成的$250億交易證明資金可取得，舊券卻顯示反覆供給如何重新定價信用強的借款人。

能同時使用公私募貸款的公司，正透過競爭降低利息。Catalent週三以$41億美元及歐元定期貸款，置換Ares與Blue Owl直接貸款，節省約225個基點。第2季銀行從私募信貸取得9筆、共$45億交易，反向移動則3筆、共$13億。到7月中，全年兩方向較接近，轉向銀行$92億、轉向直接貸款人約$90億，但最近一季偏向聯貸。

銀行工商貸款第2季年化成長14.2%，一年前4.4%。槓桿貸款規則放寬有幫助，企業發展公司則面對贖回與資產減記。私募貸款人仍能提供速度及確定性，聯貸買方也可拒絕不佳條件，先前Baker Tilly撤案就是例子。優勢最大的是能讓兩個市場競價的借款人，而非只依賴單一資金來源者。

困境資本結構與溫和的整體市場表現相距甚遠。Pyramid Management尋求以不到面額20%的價格，買回Destiny USA的$4.3億房貸；若完成，損失將超過$3.5億。約$2.35億市政稅收替代付款債券，即PILOT債，在結構上優先於CMBS；房貸債務中另有$2.15億次順位債，原始評等為AAA。出租率及銷售改善，仍不足以抵銷估值約75%的下跌、層層請求權與更高再融資成本。

QVC結束第11章重整，取得2032年到期、票息10%的$12億債權轉換債券，以及$6億資產擔保融資，總債務減少逾$50億。新債把破產前請求權轉成重整後公司的債務，不是新初級市場買方以現金建立的普通訂單簿。重整提供資金支撐的營運空間，10%票息則顯示持續成本。

San Juan規模小得多的市政發行，卻獲得異常強勁需求。逾50家機構，對$1.21億一般責任債下單約$22億。2051年到期、票息5%的免稅券，以4.90%殖利率定價，比市政基準高58個基點，隨後交易約4.77%。評等Baa3及BBB+，由指定不動產與銷售稅收入支持；2025財政年度特別不動產稅收入$1.016億，對應有擔保債務本息$5,350萬。罕見的波多黎各投資級供給，以及可辨認的收入支撐，使交易與其他風險不同。

韓國一個AI受惠者則成為信用買方。市場人士估計，SK Hynix今年投入KRW10兆至KRW40兆於本地債券及商業本票，現金與約當現金季增62%至KRW88兆。晶片獲利及$265億ADR籌資，使其在通常由金融機構主導的市場，買進金融及政府相關票券。範圍是估計而非經查核的流量，但顯示AI現金生成，也可能在其他地方的AI借款潮之外創造需求。

## 外國投資人衡量美債以外的選擇

Wellington在全球策略減少美債，並將旗下$60億World Bond Fund的部分配置轉向長期德債，理由是ECB通膨紀律更清楚、德國財政可信度較強。德國30年期接近3.5%，而美國30年期期限溢酬達2013年以來最高，形成替代選擇。單一經理人的行動不代表全市場流量，卻說明美債一天反彈，未必能恢復長期配置需求。

到週五早上，日圓已吐回接近一半干預漲幅。美元兌日圓約158.45，先前干預後曾到155.23，行動前則接近164。估計美日兩天投入約$870億，仍未克服利差、日本債務疑慮及利差交易需求。交換市場給予9月日本銀行升息約60%的機率，持久匯率支持仍部分取決於更高日本利率，或較溫和的聯準會路徑。

操作也引發協調問題。美國賣出歐元、而非美元來買日圓，事後才通知ECB，使部分歐洲官員擔心偏離慣例。日本表示未來可用美債擔保向FIMA借款，有助限制直接賣券，卻未解決反覆干預對準備管理的影響，以及更高國內殖利率的吸引力。

日本機構面對高殖利率的結果不同。GPIF第2季日本債報酬−1.1%，配置比重由3月26.91%降至25.59%。總資產在紀錄JPY24.1兆獲利後，達JPY317.76兆；外債報酬3.1%，國內外股票都有雙位數漲幅。這是季度結果，不是週五流量，但顯示最大退休基金尚未因JGB殖利率提高而增加日債權重。

四大壽險公司國內債未實現損失，在截至6月三個月增加7%至JPY15.13兆、約$960億。負債配對通常支持持有到期，但保單解約可能迫使賣出；監理機關表示損失已影響會計及流動性。高殖利率可吸引新投資，也同時限制低利率時期累積部位的彈性。

經濟數據同樣分歧。中國7月出口增23.9%，晶片增117%、電腦67%、汽車60%，協助彌補國內需求弱勢。菲律賓第2季GDP年增率由2.8%降至2.3%，低於預估中位數2.9%，消費及投資均轉弱。一邊透過AI週期擴張出口，另一邊卻同時面對成長放緩與偏高通膨。

英國官員警告，透過公共金融機構為投資借款，可能符合偏好的淨金融負債規則，卻仍增加傳統定義的債務、借款及公債發行。Resolution Foundation估計，額外借GBP100億，將增加GBP5億利息成本，而公共債務已近GDP的100%。不同財政分類，不能消除政府現金需求。

墨西哥7月整體通膨由3.37%降至3.12%，符合預期；核心由4.03%降至3.95%，接近預估3.94%。服務仍為4.36%，已連續56個月高於4%。央行維持6.50%後，這份數據提供更多整體通膨下降證據，卻未明顯緩和謹慎指引背後的國內持續性。

## 南非受惠財政改善，喀麥隆承受接班風險

美國殖利率及美元下降，帶動新興硬通貨債報酬。EMB漲0.31%，15年期以上美元主權債指數漲0.14%，美元指數跌0.37%至99.60。兩項債券指標一個月仍各跌0.73%、1.54%。共同日內環境有利，各國進展卻更分化。

南非主權溢價收窄至約102個基點，接近墨西哥、低於羅馬尼亞；5年期CDS降至約120個基點，為15年低點。外資8月淨買本地公債ZAR236億，使2026流入達ZAR620億。財政部預期債務本財政年度在GDP的77.3%見頂後下降，IMF則預估明年79.7%。基本財政盈餘與規劃中的法定財政規則，須進一步證明市場近似投資級的定價合理。

喀麥隆則有治理折價。總統Paul Biya自6月7日不在國內，接班仍未定，憲法移轉機制下的副總統職位也無人。2033年債週五殖利率9.53%，自他離開以來升約70個基點，2031年則升約50個基點。兩個月喀麥隆跌0.6%，加彭漲1%、廣泛新興美元債指數漲0.4%。政治交接不確定性，壓過美債提供的共同利多。

巴西尋求每年最多$350億國際發行授權，引發供給疑慮，財政部長官Daniel Leal則解釋這是彈性，不是發行目標。外債約占聯邦債務4%，長期目標7%，今年已在海外籌約$100億。逾$3,000億準備、浮動匯率及深厚國內市場，減輕了以往債務危機的幣別錯配；但缺乏投資級評等，仍限制更大發行日程的買方基礎。

幣別分散已實際發生。巴西發行EUR50億，是最大一筆國際交易，也是十多年來首次歐元發行；計畫中的熊貓債，2026年可籌最多CNY50億。兩者階段不同：歐元交易已完成，人民幣發行及更廣授權則提供未來選項。

坦尚尼亞透過規則建立市場准入。政府債標售向所有非居民開放，並開始公布每日主權殖利率曲線，改善貸款及企業債定價。國內借款規劃TZS3.27兆，比前一年高近11%，另可能發行最多$5億歐洲債券。融資需求增加時，接下來要看更廣資格與較佳參考價格，能否帶來持久參與。

## 股市歡迎觀望，商品卻未確認通膨紓解

S&P 500漲0.62%、Nasdaq 100漲1.19%、半導體漲2.56%，伴隨殖利率下降及VIX降至14.90。美元跌0.37%至99.60，符合9月升息信念減弱。投資人把就業報告解讀為觀望空間，而非需求立即崩落。

油價未加入這種通膨紓解解讀。WTI漲1.15%至$78.18，布蘭特漲1.29%至$83.55，雖然兩者一週仍跌逾7%。黃金漲2.33%至$4,340.70，週漲7.20%。美元弱勢有幫助，能源與地緣政治不確定性也仍存在，10年期損益兩平通膨率的小幅下降與這種混合情況一致。

投資級、高收益及新興債均上漲，卻未消除個別發行人問題。股市新高與強勁基金流入，可以和較寬的科技舊券利差、商場債務嚴重預期損失並存。有資金，不等於每個借款人都能取得同樣有利條件。

## 通膨與標售接替就業成為焦點

週三7月CPI預估整體月增0.1%，前值下降0.4%；核心月增0.2%、年增2.5%。服務較弱、月底能源傳導有限，將強化延後9月升息的理由。若意外偏高，就會檢驗Barkin的條件式觀望，並提醒市場週五債券漲勢大部分來自實質殖利率，而非通膨補償下降。

$1,250億季度再融資分別檢驗曲線不同部位：週二$580億3年期接續聯準會路徑重估；週三$420億10年期接在CPI之後；週四$250億30年期以接近5.20%的指示殖利率，面對長端溢價。配置、讓利及後續交易，將顯示這些價格能否吸引足夠需求，未來可能調整年期組合不能預先回答。

信用方面，可追蹤Alphabet新券與2月舊券、下一筆大型雲端或資料中心交易的讓利，以及Accuris計畫中$7億直接貸款人再融資。舊券穩定、新條件有競爭力，代表$5,400億TMT供給展望可能正在被消化；配售後反覆擴大利差，則顯示需求雖在，代價卻由新舊借款人與持有人持續承擔。

overall_summary.headline: 就業減少推遲升息預期，股市再創紀錄
overall_summary.session_narrative:
非農減少23,000人、前期下修103,000人，但參與率降低使失業率降至4.1%。2年期殖利率下降6個基點至4.19%，10年期降4個基點至4.65%。9月升息機率降向40%，年底前一次仍完全計價。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Payroll losses push back hike bets as stocks reach a record

## The jobs surprise favors short Treasuries

Treasuries rallied after July payrolls fell 23,000 and substantial downward revisions showed hiring had been weaker than previously reported. The two-year yield fell 6 basis points to 4.19%, leading declines of 5 basis points at five years, 4 at ten and 3 at 30. Markets reduced the probability of a September Fed increase to about 40%, from close to 60% before the release.

The report was weaker than its headline alone: May and June payrolls were revised down by a combined 103,000. Yet unemployment fell to 4.1% as participation declined, and wage growth slowed. Fewer jobs and lower unemployment were not contradictory results; people leaving the labor force helped keep the jobless rate down. The data reduced the urgency of tightening without establishing that labor slack would now be sufficient to bring inflation back to target.

Risk markets welcomed the additional room for Fed patience. The S&P 500 gained 0.62% to a record, the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.19% and VIX fell to 14.90. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin described employment as being in a weak balance and said wages were not currently adding to price pressure, while retaining the option of higher rates if inflation accelerated.

Oil rose rather than reinforcing the bond rally. Most of the ten-year yield's decline to 4.65% came through a 3-basis-point fall in the real yield to 2.40%; inflation compensation eased just 1 basis point to 2.25%. A year-end hike remained fully priced, and next week's large Treasury auctions still awaited buyers. Friday gave the front end more relief than the long end.

## Revisions change the labor picture; CPI comes next

The curve reversed Thursday's flattening. Five-year yields fell to 4.35%, ten-year yields to 4.65% and the 30-year to 5.19%. The 2s10s spread widened 2 basis points to 46 and 2s30s widened 3 to 100. Yields from two through ten years were down 9–10 basis points over the week, compared with 8 at 30 years. Long yields still stood 10–14 basis points above month-earlier levels from ten to 30 years.

The 23,000 payroll decline and 103,000 combined revisions both weakened the case for an immediate increase. Lower participation, however, was part of the reason unemployment fell to 4.1%. Slower wage growth helped the inflation outlook, but the combination was not the same as a broad rise in available workers or a clear release of capacity pressure.

Traders unwound SOFR-option hedges against two increases by year-end as September hike odds fell about 20 percentage points to roughly 40%. One increase remained fully priced by year-end, with additional protection against a second move in 2027. The adjustment was largely to timing. Limited forward guidance from Chairman Kevin Warsh leaves each release capable of changing that timetable substantially.

Barkin, a nonvoter this year, gave the patient interpretation a clearer rationale. In a low-hire market, he saw employment in a weak balance, no current wage inflation and little contribution from labor to price pressure. He had called the degree of restraint a close question the previous week and still left open an increase if inflation accelerated. His view did not erase the three July dissents for a quarter-point hike; it explained why weaker labor conditions could justify waiting for prices before acting.

The New York Fed's July consumer survey offered a mixed companion to the payroll report. One-year inflation expectations edged from 3.7% to 3.6%, while three-year expectations stayed at 3.3% and five-year expectations at 3.0%. The perceived probability of finding a new job if unemployed rose to 46.2%, its highest this year. At the same time, respondents became more likely to expect higher unemployment and slightly more worried about losing their own jobs. Broader concern about the labor market had not produced a collapse in perceived re-employment prospects.

At ten years, the real yield's 3-basis-point decline accounted for most of the nominal rally. The breakeven's 1-basis-point fall only partly reversed Thursday's 4-basis-point increase. Over a month, the real yield remained 10 basis points higher and inflation compensation was unchanged. Investors were still demanding more real return than a month earlier, even after substantially revising the near-term employment outlook.

Treasury supply now provides a separate test. Next week brings $58 billion of three-year notes on Tuesday, $42 billion of ten-year notes on Wednesday and $25 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday. Indicated yields before the sales pointed to the highest three- and ten-year auction levels since early 2025. At 30 years, the indicated 5.20% exceeded every auction result since August 2001. Those levels may attract buyers, but the sales have not yet established demand.

Strategists also differed on the implication of Treasury's new language about evaluating future issuance “changes” rather than “increases.” Some saw room to cut 20- and 30-year sizes while concentrating funding growth in two- to ten-year notes; others thought the borrowing requirement made long-end reductions implausible. No reduction has been announced. Changing maturities could redistribute supply pressure without reducing the total cash that Treasury needs.

## More technology supply, more competition for refinancing

Credit participated in the rally. LQD rose 0.18%, HYG gained 0.19% and JNK added 0.21%; long-maturity US corporate indexes advanced about 0.20%–0.22%. High-yield funds received $4 billion during the week, the largest inflow in two years, and speculative-grade spreads returned near their tightest levels of 2026. The appetite for credit risk was substantial, even where repeated issuance was weighing on individual sectors.

JPMorgan raised its 2026 technology, media and telecommunications issuance forecast from $450 billion to $540 billion. Hyperscalers account for an expected $317 billion, including $85 billion of data-center project financing that could exceed $100 billion if the identified pipeline proceeds. The forecast excluding hyperscalers nearly doubled from $78 billion to about $146 billion, largely to incorporate Nvidia's $25 billion June sale. The projected supply is broader than any single week's calendar.

Existing bonds show the cost of absorbing it. Some hyperscaler spreads widened around 15 basis points as investors confronted $75 billion of unexpected June and July issuance. They recovered over the past week, but limited visibility on timing remained a problem. Alphabet's February 30-year bond traded above 100 basis points over Treasuries, against roughly 83 at issue and a June low near 70. The newly completed $25 billion sale demonstrated access; the seasoned bond showed how recurring supply can reprice an otherwise strong borrower.

Borrowers with access to both public and private loans were using competition to cut interest expense. Catalent refinanced Ares and Blue Owl direct loans with $4.1 billion of dollar and euro term loans on Wednesday, saving about 225 basis points. In the second quarter, banks took nine deals worth $4.5 billion from private credit, while three deals worth $1.3 billion moved in the other direction. Through mid-July, year-to-date totals were more balanced—$9.2 billion toward banks and roughly $9 billion toward direct lenders—but the latest quarter favored the syndicated route.

Bank commercial and industrial lending grew at a 14.2% annualized rate in the second quarter, compared with 4.4% a year earlier. Eased leveraged-loan rules helped, while business-development companies faced redemptions and markdowns. Private lenders still offer speed and certainty; syndicated buyers can still reject unattractive terms, as Baker Tilly's previously withdrawn transaction showed. The opportunity is greatest for borrowers able to make the two markets compete, rather than those dependent on one source of money.

Distressed structures remained far removed from the benign broad-market picture. Pyramid Management sought to buy back the $430 million Destiny USA mortgage for less than 20 cents on the dollar, implying more than $350 million of losses if completed. About $235 million of municipal payment-in-lieu-of-taxes, or PILOT, bonds rank structurally ahead of the CMBS. The mortgage debt includes $215 million of subordinate bonds originally rated AAA. Better occupancy and sales had not overcome the roughly 75% decline in appraised value, the layered claims or the higher refinancing cost.

QVC emerged from Chapter 11 with $1.2 billion of take-back notes due in 2032 at 10% and a $600 million asset-based facility, reducing total debt by more than $5 billion. The notes convert pre-bankruptcy claims into debt of the reorganized company; they are not an ordinary cash orderbook from new primary-market buyers. The restructuring supplies a funded runway, with the 10% coupon showing the continuing cost.

San Juan drew exceptional demand for a much smaller municipal sale. More than 50 firms placed about $2.2 billion of orders for $121 million of general-obligation bonds. Tax-exempt 2051 debt with a 5% coupon priced at 4.90%, 58 basis points above the municipal benchmark, and subsequently traded near 4.77%. Rated Baa3 and BBB+, the issue is backed by pledged property- and sales-tax revenue. Fiscal 2025 special-property-tax collections were $101.6 million against $53.5 million of secured debt service. Rare investment-grade Puerto Rico supply and identifiable revenue support helped the deal stand apart.

In South Korea, an AI beneficiary was itself becoming a substantial credit buyer. Market participants estimated SK Hynix had put KRW10 trillion–KRW40 trillion into local bonds and commercial paper during the year, as cash and equivalents increased 62% quarter on quarter to KRW88 trillion. Chip earnings and $26.5 billion of ADR proceeds were supporting purchases of financial and government-related paper in a market usually dominated by institutions. The range is an estimate, not an audited flow, but it shows how AI cash generation can create demand alongside the borrowing wave elsewhere.

## Foreign investors weigh alternatives to Treasuries

Wellington reduced Treasury exposure across global strategies and shifted part of its $6 billion World Bond Fund toward long German debt, citing clearer ECB inflation discipline and stronger German fiscal credibility. German 30-year yields near 3.5% offered an alternative as the US 30-year term premium reached its highest since 2013. One manager's decision is not a market-wide flow, but it illustrates why a daily Treasury rally need not restore longer-term allocation demand.

The yen had surrendered nearly half its intervention gains by Friday morning. It traded near 158.45 per dollar after reaching 155.23, having approached 164 before the joint US-Japan operation. Estimated intervention spending of about $87 billion over two days had not overcome the rate differential, Japan's debt concerns and carry demand. Swaps assigned about a 60% chance to a September BOJ increase, keeping a higher Japanese policy path—or a softer Fed path—relevant to lasting currency support.

The operation also raised coordination questions. The US sold euros rather than dollars to buy yen and notified the ECB afterward, concerning some European officials about a departure from convention. Japan's stated ability to use FIMA against Treasury collateral in future operations can limit outright sales. It does not settle the reserve-management implications of repeated intervention or the pull of higher domestic bond yields.

Japanese institutions were experiencing those higher yields differently. GPIF's Japanese bonds returned −1.1% in the second quarter, and their portfolio weight fell from 26.91% in March to 25.59%. Total assets reached JPY317.76 trillion after a record JPY24.1 trillion gain; foreign bonds returned 3.1%, while domestic and foreign equities had double-digit gains. These quarterly results are not Friday flows, but they show that higher JGB yields had not yet translated into a larger domestic-bond weight at the largest pension fund.

At the four largest life insurers, unrealized domestic-bond losses rose 7% in the three months through June to JPY15.13 trillion, or $96 billion. Liability matching normally supports holding to maturity, but policy cancellations can force sales. The regulator said the losses were already affecting accounting and liquidity. Higher yields may attract new investment while restricting the flexibility of portfolios accumulated at lower rates.

Economic releases also pointed in different directions. China's July exports increased 23.9%, led by chips at 117%, computers at 67% and autos at 60%, helping cushion weak domestic demand. Philippine second-quarter GDP slowed from 2.8% to 2.3% year on year, below the 2.9% median forecast, as consumption and investment weakened. Strong AI-linked export activity in one economy contrasted with softer growth and elevated inflation in the other.

UK officials warned that investment borrowing through public financial institutions could satisfy the preferred net-financial-liabilities rule while still increasing conventional debt, borrowing and gilt issuance. The Resolution Foundation estimated another GBP10 billion of borrowing would add GBP500 million to interest costs, with public debt already near 100% of GDP. A different fiscal classification does not remove the government's cash requirement.

Mexico's July headline inflation eased from 3.37% to 3.12%, in line with expectations, while core fell from 4.03% to 3.95%, close to the 3.94% estimate. Services stayed at 4.36%, above 4% for 56 consecutive months. The release supplied more evidence of headline disinflation after Banxico's 6.50% hold, but little relief from the domestic persistence behind its cautious guidance.

## Fiscal gains lift South Africa; succession weighs on Cameroon

Lower US yields and a weaker dollar helped EM hard-currency returns. EMB gained 0.31% and the 15-year-plus dollar sovereign index rose 0.14%, while the Dollar Index fell 0.37% to 99.60. Both bond measures remained lower over a month, by 0.73% and 1.54%, respectively. Country developments were more differentiated than the supportive daily backdrop.

South Africa's sovereign premium narrowed to about 102 basis points, near Mexico and below Romania. Five-year CDS reached a 15-year low near 120 basis points. Foreign investors bought a net ZAR23.6 billion of local government bonds in August, taking 2026 inflows to ZAR62 billion. Treasury expected debt to peak at 77.3% of GDP this fiscal year and then fall; the IMF projected 79.7% next year. Primary surpluses and a planned statutory fiscal rule now need to justify the market's investment-grade-like pricing.

Cameroon faced a governance discount. President Paul Biya's absence since June 7 left succession unresolved, with no vice president in place under the constitutional transfer mechanism. Its 2033 bond yielded 9.53% on Friday, roughly 70 basis points higher since his departure, while the 2031 yield was up about 50. Cameroon lost 0.6% over two months, against Gabon's 1% gain and 0.4% for a broad EM dollar index. Political-transition uncertainty was outweighing the common benefit from Treasuries.

Brazil sought authority for as much as $35 billion of annual global issuance, prompting concern about supply. Treasury Secretary Daniel Leal described it as flexibility, not an issuance target. External bonds are about 4% of federal debt, against a longer-run objective of 7%, and the country has raised roughly $10 billion abroad this year. More than $300 billion of reserves, a floating exchange rate and a deep domestic market reduce the currency mismatch of its earlier debt crisis. The absence of an investment-grade rating still restricts the buyer base for a larger calendar.

Currency diversification is already visible. Brazil sold EUR5 billion in its largest global transaction and first euro issue in more than a decade. A planned panda bond could raise as much as CNY5 billion in 2026. These are different stages of financing: the euro deal is complete, while the yuan issue and broader authorization provide future options.

Tanzania is building access through market rules. It opened government-securities auctions to all nonresidents and began publishing a daily sovereign yield curve to improve pricing for loans and corporate debt. Planned domestic borrowing is TZS3.27 trillion, nearly 11% more than the previous year, with a possible Eurobond of up to $500 million. The next question is whether broader eligibility and better reference prices bring lasting participation as financing needs increase.

## Stocks welcome patience, while commodities resist disinflation

The S&P 500's 0.62% gain, the Nasdaq 100's 1.19% rise and a 2.56% semiconductor advance accompanied lower yields and VIX at 14.90. The dollar's 0.37% fall to 99.60 matched reduced conviction in a September hike. Investors read the jobs report as room for patience rather than an immediate collapse in demand.

Oil did not join that disinflationary interpretation. WTI rose 1.15% to $78.18 and Brent gained 1.29% to $83.55, though both remained more than 7% lower for the week. Gold advanced 2.33% to $4,340.70, a weekly gain of 7.20%. Dollar weakness helped, while energy and geopolitical uncertainty remained relevant. The small decline in ten-year breakevens was consistent with that mixed commodity picture.

Investment-grade, high-yield and EM bonds all gained, but those returns did not remove issuer-specific problems. Record equities and strong fund inflows coexisted with wider seasoned technology spreads and severe expected losses on mall debt. Available capital was not the same as equally favorable financing for every borrower.

## Inflation and auctions take over from payrolls

Wednesday's July CPI forecast calls for a 0.1% headline increase after a 0.4% decline, with core rising 0.2% on the month and 2.5% from a year earlier. Softer services and limited late-month energy pass-through would reinforce the case for delaying the next hike beyond September. An upside surprise would test Barkin's conditional patience and remind markets that most of Friday's bond rally came from real yields, not lower inflation compensation.

The $125 billion refunding sequence tests different parts of the curve: Tuesday's $58 billion three-year sale follows the Fed-path repricing; Wednesday's $42 billion ten-year sale follows CPI; Thursday's $25 billion 30-year sale confronts the long-end premium at an indicated yield near 5.20%. Investor allocations, concessions and subsequent trading will show whether those yields attract sufficient demand. Possible future changes in the maturity mix do not answer that question in advance.

In credit, investors can follow Alphabet's new and February bonds, concessions on the next hyperscaler or data-center issue, and Accuris's planned $700 million refinancing of direct lenders. Stable outstanding bonds and competitive new terms would suggest the $540 billion TMT supply outlook is being accommodated. Repeated widening after allocation would show that demand remains available only at an increasing cost to existing and new borrowers.
